correctness.rationale: The left/right angle updates follow from splitting the largest angle; the child recurrence has exhaustive 3-by-2 branch cases. The minimum of the half-largest/middle/least triple cannot decrease. On the affine decomposition of the normalized 2D shape simplex, the spread defects are convex. The supplied exact rational checker enumerates all 31 nonempty branch-order/spread cells and 61 vertices, with zero positive two-step gap, which proves the infinite-parameter inequalities by vertex extremality. A nondegenerate isosceles family gives equality at factor 3/4. Conditional expectations and Markov inequality then give the finite-level concentration estimate. value.rationale: Quantitative finite-level shape concentration and dependence on changing symbolic child choices are substantive problems motivated by recent largest-angle triangle refinement literature. The universal sharp 3/4 factor identifies an exact nonlinear contraction mechanism that a mere strict-decrease statement does not supply; the deduced explicit exponential concentration bound evaluates the proportion of poorly shaped descendants at every depth. This is an all-shapes structural theorem, not an arbitrary small sample or a routine known-table computation. The 7/8 bound is not asserted globally rate-optimal.
